- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.7) and model forecasts are trending upward, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If recent true outcomes show sharp downward spikes after high peaks, model should adjust downward with lagged momentum correction.  
- When official event net supply is negative and bullish sentiment is high, model should not ignore policy-driven mean reversion — forecast should slightly undershoot peak expectations.  
- If model forecasts are flat or slowly rising while true outcomes show rapid decline, introduce early downward bias to account for sentiment-driven volatility.  
- For 30-day horizons, if sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model should avoid linear extrapolation and incorporate swing-based smoothing.  
- When supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model should not assume continuation — forecast should be conservative and slightly below historical mean.  
- If model forecasts are consistently above true outcomes in early days of a 30-day window, apply downward bias to correct for overconfidence in short-term momentum.
